old_caption:
The video begins with a close-up shot of a white piece of paper placed on a dark surface. The paper contains handwritten text and diagrams. At the top left corner, the letters "CD" are written in purple marker. Below this, there is a horizontal line followed by the word "LABEL" written in orange marker. Underneath "LABEL," the word "LACQUER" is written in black marker. Further down, the word "PLASTIC" is written in green marker. To the right of these labels, there is one set of measurements: "METAL 50-100 nm," written in green marker.

Below the labels and measurements, there is a single wavy line drawn in black marker, resembling a cross-section or diagram of a layered structure. The labels "LACQUER" and "PLASTIC" are positioned above the line, corresponding to their respective layers. The camera remains mostly static, then moves slightly to the left, revealing a CD next to the paper, with light reflecting off its surface.
original_wisa_caption:
The video begins with a close-up shot of a white piece of paper placed on a dark surface. The paper contains handwritten text and diagrams. At the top left corner, the letters "EB" are written in purple marker. Below this, there is a horizontal line followed by the word "LABEL" written in orange marker. Underneath "LABEL," the word "LACQUER" is written in black marker. Further down, the word "PLASTIC" is written in green marker. To the right of these labels, there are two sets of measurements: "METAL 50-100 nm" and "PLASTIC 50-100 nm," both written in green marker.

Below the labels and measurements, there are several rectangular shapes drawn in black marker, resembling a cross-section or diagram of a layered structure. These rectangles are labeled with "LACQUER" and "PLASTIC" at the bottom, corresponding to their respective layers.
caption:
A white hand-drawn card rests on a dark textured surface, showing a labeled cross-section diagram of a compact disc. The purple heading reads CD above black boundary lines, while orange LABEL and LACQUER sit over a gray METAL 50-100nm note. A stepped, foil-like strip catches the light between the metal line and the green PLASTIC label, and red LASER text with two upward arrows points from below. Through much of the clip the card stays nearly centered. Only small perspective and lighting shifts occur, and the drawn strip keeps reflecting bright spots.

Later the view blurs and the card appears to shift toward the right edge, and a real rainbow-colored disc appears on the left. The actual CD shows its central hole and a bright white reflection on its upper surface. A blue-purple glow appears near its left edge, while a hand enters from the right beside the card.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.
